grammar.title: Tu vs. vous
grammar.explanation: French has two forms of 'you': 'tu' (informal, friends/family/children) and 'vous' (formal, strangers, elders, or plural). Verb endings change with each: 'Comment vas-tu ?' vs 'Comment allez-vous ?'.

examples.text: Bonjour, je m'appelle Louis. Et vous ?
examples.translation: Hello, my name is Louis. And you?
Pleased to meet you! How are you?

content.tip: Default to 'vous' with anyone you don't know well — switching to 'tu' too soon can sound overly familiar.

grammar.title: Soixante-dix and beyond
grammar.explanation: French counts 70-99 by addition/multiplication: 70 = soixante-dix ('sixty-ten'), 80 = quatre-vingts ('four-twenties'), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix ('four-twenty-ten'). Belgian/Swiss French often use septante/nonante instead.

examples.text: Combien ça coûte ? — Ça coûte vingt euros.
examples.translation: How much is it? — It's twenty euros.

content.tip: Drill 70-99 separately from the rest — they trip up nearly every learner at first.

grammar.title: Partitive articles (du, de la, des)
grammar.explanation: Use du (masc.), de la (fem.), or des (plural) for 'some' with food and drink: 'Je voudrais du pain' (I'd like some bread), 'de la confiture' (some jam).

examples.text: Je voudrais du pain et de la confiture.
examples.translation: I would like some bread and some jam.

content.tip: Order your actual morning drink in French in your head before you make it, every day this week.

grammar.title: Passé composé with avoir vs. être
grammar.explanation: Most verbs form the past with avoir + past participle: 'j'ai mangé'. A small set of motion/state verbs (aller, venir, naître, mourir, partir, arriver, and their compounds) use être instead, and the participle agrees in gender/number: 'elle est allée'.

examples.text: Hier, je suis allé au marché et j'ai acheté des fruits.
examples.translation: Yesterday I went to the market and bought some fruit.

content.tip: Memorize the être-verbs as the 'house' story: they're often taught arranged like a house floor plan — it makes the list stick.
